risk_if_not_implemented: Without Monitoring for Third-Party Information Disclosure, supplier and External Service Provider (ESP) weaknesses, incidents or failures may propagate into the organization's environment unmanaged. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Undetected / Delayed Detection of Adverse Activity (R-SA-1), Loss of Confidentiality (R-IP-2), and most likely increases susceptibility to Malicious Cyber Activity (MT-2), Human Error (MT-9), Technical / Mechanical Failure (MT-10), Fraud, Corruption and/or Intentional Criminal Conduct (MT-14), Workforce Shortage / Loss of Critical Skills / Labor Disruption (MT-25).

compensating_control_1.name: Monitoring For Information Disclosure
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to monitor for evidence of unauthorized exfiltration or disclosure of non-public information.
compensating_control_1.justification: Monitoring For Information Disclosure (MON-19) provides detective monitoring capability that compensates for the absence of Monitoring for Third-Party Information Disclosure (MON-19.1) by identifying unauthorized, anomalous, or non-compliant activity that the primary control would have prevented. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Cross-Organizational Monitoring
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to coordinate sanitized event logs and security-relevant telemetry among external organizations to identify anomalous events when that data is shared across organizational boundaries, without giving away sensitive or critical business data.
compensating_control_2.justification: Cross-Organizational Monitoring (MON-36.1) provides detective monitoring capability that compensates for the absence of Monitoring for Third-Party Information Disclosure (MON-19.1) by identifying unauthorized, anomalous, or non-compliant activity that the primary control would have prevented. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
